venue.name: Remote Passages Marine Excursions
venue.description: Remote Passages Marine Excursions is a family run marine tour operator working out of a boathouse at 51 Wharf Street in Tofino, on Clayoquot Sound. It has run Zodiac wildlife tours on the west coast since 1986 and now offers whale and sea otter watching, coastal bear watching, a day trip to the Hot Springs Cove thermal pools, guided sea kayaking day trips and a water taxi walk to the Big Tree Trail on Meares Island. The fleet is rigid hull Zodiacs carrying 10 to 12 passengers plus one covered cabin vessel, the Star Light, which carries up to 12 and has a heated cabin and a washroom aboard. A group discount is offered for parties of 6 or more, and groups of that size are asked to book by phone.

facility_notes.has_washrooms: Dedicated boathouse with reception, dress-in area, restrooms, and hot drinks after outings. The covered vessel also features an on-board washroom.
facility_notes.bus_parking: Free parking for cars. Yes, parking can be provided for cars while space is available. The good news is the parking is free!

restrictions: A program marked * is not suitable for expectant mothers, or for persons with back problems. This mark is on the Whales & Sea Otters tours, on both vessels, and on the Hot Springs Explorer.
Relevant medical conditions (such as back or neck problems, heart conditions, pregnancy or osteoporosis) must be disclosed to Remote Passages prior to signing this waiver.
Parents and legal guardians of any Participants under the age of 19 agree to be bound by the terms set forth herein, and the waiver must be signed on site before an activity.
On the Zodiac the child fare is listed for 5 to 12 year olds; the covered cabin vessel the Star Light is the one described as suitable for passengers aged 3 years and older.
The Hot Springs Explorer requires a minimum of 6 to launch.
Reserves right to refuse passage, cancel departures, substitute vessels for any reason.
venue.seasonal_notes: The booking request form on the contact page accepts departure dates from April 1 to October 15. Sea kayaking day trips are described as running daily April to mid-October, and the Meares Island and sea kayaking tours list departure times as April to October. The Hot Springs Explorer is described as March or April through October. The about page separately describes the wildlife viewing season as February to November. Grey whales are described as feeding along the coast from their March return until October, humpbacks returning each spring, and transient Killer whales visiting throughout the year.

programs.name: Whales & Sea Otters, Zodiac
programs.description: A two and a half to three hour wildlife tour in an open rigid hull Zodiac, departing daily and travelling through both sheltered and open coast water to Grey whale feeding areas, with interpretive stops for coastal wildlife and rainforest. Adults pay $169 and the child fare of $139 is listed for ages 5 to 12, so under fives are not priced for this vessel. A $10 fuel surcharge, a $3 wildlife and ecosystem research and education fee and 5% GST are added at payment. A group discount is offered for parties of 6 or more, and the contact page asks parties of 6 or more to phone. The rate table does not say how large the discount is.
programs.what_children_do: Sit in padded seats with backrests in an open inflatable boat, zipped into an issued all weather suit, while the boat runs out through the sound and then stops so everyone can watch for Grey whales, sea otters, sea lions, seals, porpoise and bald eagles. Between stops the boat travels fast, and there are interpretive stops along the coast and the rainforest shore.
programs.our_note: This is the open boat, so the children are out in wind and spray for the whole two and a half to three hours with nowhere inside to warm up. The child fare here starts at age 5, so a group of three and four year olds needs the covered cabin vessel instead. Ask what the group rate actually comes to when you phone, because the size of the discount is not published anywhere.
programs.practical_summary: The boathouse has restrooms, a dress-in area and hot drinks after the trip, and car parking is free. Only the covered cabin vessel is described as having a washroom aboard, and bus parking, a lunch space and any wet weather backup are not stated, so it is worth a call.
programs.extra_fees_note: The following are added at time of payment: $10 Fuel Surcharge, $3 for wildlife and ecosystem research and education, 5% GST.
programs.cancellation_note: 48 hour change/cancellation policy (groups may vary). If a departure is cancelled or schedules altered due to conditions you may reschedule or collect a full refund.

programs.name: Whales & Sea Otters, cabin vessel
programs.description: The same two and a half to three hour whale and sea otter tour, run daily aboard the Star Light, a covered vessel carrying up to 12 with a heated cabin, glass all around with window defog, a large back deck and a washroom on board. Adults pay $169 and the child fare of $139 is listed for ages 3 to 12. The vessels page says the Star Light is suitable for passengers aged 3 years and older. A $10 fuel surcharge, a $3 wildlife and ecosystem research and education fee and 5% GST are added at payment. A group discount is offered for parties of 6 or more, who are asked to phone.
programs.what_children_do: Sit inside a heated cabin with glass all around and watch for Grey whales, sea otters, sea lions, seals, porpoise and bald eagles, then step out onto the back deck when the boat stops for a closer look. Every passenger wears a self inflating collar.
programs.our_note: This is the one to ask for with a preschool group. It is the only vessel the site describes as suitable from age 3, it is heated, it has a washroom aboard and the children can go inside when they have had enough of the wind. It carries 12, so a group of more than ten children plus adults will not fit in one sailing.
programs.practical_summary: There is a washroom on this vessel and restrooms, a dress-in area and hot drinks at the boathouse, and car parking is free. Bus parking, a lunch space and how a wet day is handled are not stated, so it is worth a call.
programs.extra_fees_note: The following are added at time of payment: $10 Fuel Surcharge, $3 for wildlife and ecosystem research and education, 5% GST.
programs.cancellation_note: 48 hour change/cancellation policy (groups may vary). If a departure is cancelled or schedules altered due to conditions you may reschedule or collect a full refund.

programs.name: Coastal Bear Watch
programs.description: A two and a half hour quiet water excursion in a 24 foot Zodiac along fjord inlets, stopping in sheltered bays to watch black bears come down to the shoreline to feed on crab, clams and barnacles. The guide also talks about seals, eagles, porpoise and heron. Departures run daily but the time is set by the low tide, because that is when the bears come down to feed. Adults pay $169 and the child fare of $139 is listed for ages 5 to 12. A $10 fuel surcharge, a $3 research and education fee and 5% tax are added at payment. A group discount is offered for parties of 6 or more, and the site says discounts apply to adult rates only.
programs.what_children_do: Sit in an open inflatable boat in calm inlet water, wrapped in an issued all weather suit, while the guide idles in close to sheltered bays so everyone can watch black bears turning over rocks on the shore. The guide talks about the bears and about the seals, eagles, porpoise and heron on the way.
programs.our_note: The departure time moves with the tide rather than the clock, so you cannot pick a slot to suit nap time and you will only know the time once you phone. It is a calm water trip, which makes it the gentler of the two Zodiac tours, but the child fare still starts at age 5 and there is no cabin to get out of the weather. Bring a camera that a child can hold, because the bears stay on shore and the boat keeps its distance.
programs.practical_summary: The boathouse has restrooms, a dress-in area and hot drinks afterwards, and car parking is free. There is no washroom on the Zodiac, and bus parking, a lunch space and a wet weather backup are not stated, so it is worth a call.
programs.extra_fees_note: The following are added at time of payment: 5% Tax, $3 for marine wildlife and forest ecosystem research and education in Clayoquot Sound, $10 Fuel Surcharge. Discounts on Adult rates only.
programs.cancellation_note: 48 hour change/cancellation policy (groups may vary). If a departure is cancelled or schedules altered due to conditions you may reschedule or collect a full refund.

programs.name: Hot Springs Explorer
programs.description: A six to six and a half hour day trip running 32 km north from Tofino to Hot Springs Cove in Maquinna Provincial Park, on either an open Zodiac or the covered cabin vessel. The boat makes wildlife stops at sea lion haul outs, bald eagle lookouts and a seabird nesting island, and often stops for whales. At the dock everyone walks a 2 km wooden boardwalk trail to the natural sulphur pools, which run at about 50C. The rate is $239 for everyone, with no separate child fare published. A $4 provincial park fee, a $15 Ahousat First Nations stewardship fee, a $16 fuel surcharge, a $3 research and education fee and 5% tax are added at payment. The trip needs a minimum of 6 people to launch and departure times are given by phone.
programs.what_children_do: Ride a boat for a long stretch each way with stops to watch sea lions, eagles, seabirds and sometimes whales, then walk a two kilometre wooden boardwalk through rainforest carrying their own food and water, and soak in hot natural pools before walking the boardwalk back.
programs.our_note: This one is written up on the site as a day excursion for the energetic, and it is a long day for small children: roughly four kilometres of boardwalk on their own feet, plus hours on the water, plus a swim in water at about 50C. There is no child price, so every child pays the full $239 before fees. If you do consider it, ask for the covered vessel, because it is the one with the heated cabin and a washroom.
programs.practical_summary: The covered vessel has a washroom aboard and the boathouse has restrooms and a dress-in area, and car parking is free. You pack your own food and a litre of water per person. Bus parking and a lunch space are not stated, and the cancellation terms are stricter than the other tours, so it is worth a call.
programs.extra_fees_note: The following are added at time of payment: 5% Tax, $3 for marine wildlife and forest ecosystem research and education in Clayoquot Sound, $4 Provincial Park fee for Maquinna Marine Park, $15 Ahousat First Nations Stewardship fee, $16 Fuel Surcharge. Discounts on Adult rates only.
programs.cancellation_note: Special change/cancellation policy for this limited-availbility program: minimum 1 week notice prior to departure (groups may vary).
programs.evidence: Requires a minimum of 6 to launch

programs.name: Sea Kayaking, Islands
programs.description: A two and a half hour guided paddle from Tofino out to the outer coast islands through the protected water of Tofino harbour and nearby inlets, with stories about the Clayoquot Island characters and frequent early evening wildlife sightings. The rate is $83 plus 5% GST and a $3 research and education fee. Trips run daily from April to mid October and the departure time varies with the tide, so the same tour is sometimes scheduled as a Sunriser or a Sundowner. Every trip starts with a training session on land, no experience is needed, and the guide ratio is 6 paddlers to 1 guide with a maximum of 12 paddlers and 2 guides departing at once. All basic kayaking gear is provided, down to water shoes. A group discount is offered but the site asks you to contact them for it.
programs.what_children_do: Start on land with a paddling lesson, then sit in a single or double kayak and paddle out of Tofino harbour to the outer islands, listening to the guide's stories and watching for birds and wildlife along the way.
programs.our_note: The site's own answer on the youngest age names a For Families two and a half hour paddle for children 5 and over, but that trip is not in the rate table, so phone and ask whether this Islands paddle is the family one before you assume the ages match. Twelve paddlers is the hard ceiling for one departure, and children will almost certainly need to share a double with an adult. The start time moves with the tide, so it can land in the early evening.
programs.practical_summary: All the kayaking gear is provided, parking is free and the boathouse has restrooms, a dress-in area and hot drinks afterwards. There is no washroom once you are on the water, and lunch space, bus parking and what happens in bad weather are not stated, so it is worth a call.
programs.extra_fees_note: Add 5% GST. $3 will be added to all fares to support marine wildlife and forest ecosystem research and education in Clayoquot Sound. Discounts on Adult rates only.
programs.cancellation_note: 48 hour change/cancellation policy (groups may vary). If a departure is cancelled or schedules altered due to conditions you may reschedule or collect a full refund.
programs.evidence: Maximum number of paddlers departing at one time is 12 with 2 guides.

programs.name: Sea Kayaking, Clayoquot Explorer
programs.description: A four hour guided paddle from Tofino across to Meares Island through hidden inlets and past forested islands, including a walk with the guide on the Big Tree Trail and an introduction to Clayoquot Sound's rainforest ecology and local history. The site recommends it for persons 12 and over. The rate is $135 plus 5% GST, a $3 trail fee for the Tla-o-qui-aht Tribal Parks Society and a $3 research and education fee. Trips run daily from April to mid October, with the departure time varying according to the tide. No experience is needed and a medium level of fitness is required. The guide ratio is 6 paddlers to 1 guide, with a maximum of 12 paddlers and 2 guides departing at once.
programs.what_children_do: Learn to paddle on land first, then paddle for a couple of hours across to Meares Island, land, and walk the Big Tree Trail boardwalk among old growth cedar with the guide before paddling back. On the mudflats at low tide there are eagles and migratory birds to spot.
programs.our_note: The site recommends this for 12 and over, so it is a school age trip rather than a preschool one. Four hours of paddling plus a rainforest walk is a real day of effort, and a medium level of fitness is the stated requirement. Twelve paddlers is the ceiling for one departure, so a class will need more than one sailing.
programs.practical_summary: All the kayaking gear is provided, parking is free and the boathouse has restrooms, a dress-in area and hot drinks afterwards. There is no washroom on the water or on the trail, and lunch space, bus parking and a wet weather plan are not stated, so it is worth a call.
programs.extra_fees_note: Add 5% GST. $3 Trail fee per person on behalf of the Tla-o-qui-aht Tribal Parks Society. $3 will be added to all fares to support marine wildlife and forest ecosystem research and education in Clayoquot Sound. Discounts on Adult rates only.
programs.cancellation_note: 48 hour change/cancellation policy (groups may vary). If a departure is cancelled or schedules altered due to conditions you may reschedule or collect a full refund.

programs.name: Meares Island Big Tree Trail
programs.description: A one and a half hour trip in total: a ten minute open Zodiac water taxi ride through the harbour islands to Meares Island in the Tla-o-qui-aht Tribal Park, a walk on a handcrafted boardwalk among old growth trees up to 1600 years old, and the ride back to the boathouse. Adults pay $35 and children pay $25, plus 5% GST, a $5 trail fee for the Tla-o-qui-aht Tribal Parks Society and $1.50 for research and education. The site says a medium level of fitness is needed and that the boardwalk, though rustic in its building design, is a short walk. Departure times are given by phone and this tour is booked by contacting them rather than online.
programs.what_children_do: Ride ten minutes in an open Zodiac wearing a life jacket, land on Meares Island and walk a rustic wooden boardwalk in among giant cedar, spruce and hemlock with salal, moss and ferns underneath, then ride back.
programs.our_note: This is the shortest and cheapest thing on offer and the easiest to fit around a nap, at about an hour and a half door to door, and the boardwalk walk itself is short. No age is attached to the child fare, so ask what the youngest they will take on the water taxi is. You cannot book this one online, so allow time for a phone call, and note the trail fee is $5 a head here rather than the $3 charged on the kayak trip.
programs.practical_summary: The boathouse has restrooms, a dress-in area and hot drinks afterwards, and car parking is free. There are no washrooms on the trail, and lunch space, bus parking and what happens in heavy rain are not stated, so it is worth a call.
programs.extra_fees_note: Add 5% GST. $5 Trail fee per person on behalf of the Tla-o-qui-aht Tribal Parks Society. $1.50 will be added to all fares to support marine wildlife and forest ecosystem research and education in Clayoquot Sound.
programs.evidence: We recommend advance booking for all our tours ( contact us to book this tour).

gaps: no school, daycare or educational group programme is described anywhere on the site; the only group provision is a discount for parties of 6 or more and a phone number to call
the size of the group discount is never stated, only that it exists for parties of 6 or more and that on the bear, hot springs, kayak and Meares pages discounts apply to adult rates only

no explicit minimum age is published for the Zodiac tours; the only age figure is the 5 to 12 child fare bracket in the rate tables, which is what age_min_years rests on for the Zodiac whale and bear tours

the youngest age of 3 rests on the vessels page saying the covered cabin vessel the Star Light is suitable for passengers aged 3 years and older, and on the 3 to 12 child fare on the cabin row of the whale rate table; no minimum age is stated for the venue as a whole
the FAQ names a For Families 2 and a half hour kayak paddle for children 5 years and older, but no tour of that name appears in the sea kayaking rate table, so it is unclear which paddle it is
no age is attached to the child fare on the Meares Island Big Tree Trail tour
no minimum or child rate is published for the Hot Springs Explorer; the $239 rate appears to apply to everyone
months unknown for the whale watching and bear watching tours; their own pages give no operating season, only when the animals are present
no lead time or minimum notice for a booking is published, only a recommendation to book in advance

the tours page lists Private Tours, described only as arranging a private tour of Clayoquot's hidden gems with a link to contact them; no duration, price, age or capacity is given, so it is not recorded as a program

no capacity is published for the Coastal Bear Watch or the Hot Springs Explorer; the 12 recorded for the whale tours comes from the vessels page describing the Zodiacs as carrying 10 to 12 passengers and the cabin vessel up to 12
no chaperone or adult to child ratio is published; the 6 paddlers to 1 guide figure on the kayak tours is a guide ratio, not a supervision requirement
no indoor lunch space is described anywhere; the Hot Springs Explorer page tells you to pack your own food
no wet weather or rain backup plan is described; all weather suits and jackets are issued but no alternative to going out is mentioned
no bus or coach parking is mentioned; the site says only that free parking is available for cars while space is available
wheelchair and stroller access is not addressed anywhere on the site
no opening hours for the boathouse are published
the email address on the contact page is scrambled by JavaScript and cannot be read from the page source, so booking_email is left null; the two phone numbers are published in plain text
the Open Graph image on the home page is a Book Now button graphic hosted on a different domain rather than a photograph, so it was not used as the hero
the home page banner slideshow images are CSS background images with no alt attribute, so they were not used; the recorded images are all elements carrying the site's own alt text

the boathouse photograph on the about page carries the alt text Grey Whale Tail and the owners' portrait carries Lady in Hot Springs, so several alt attributes on that page belong to other photographs; those images were left out rather than recorded with a wrong description

conflicts.note: Their own pages give two different answers for when tours actually run. One says the season is February to November, while the booking request form will only take dates between April 1 and October 15. If you are looking at the shoulder months, worth settling when you book.

The youngest child they will take depends on which boat you get. The open Zodiac prices children from 5, and the covered cabin boat is the one they describe as suitable from age 3. Ask for the cabin boat by name when you book a group of little ones.
